summary: REDESIGN: the candidate has material approval, replay, escalation, materialization, calibration, and source-preservation defects that permit false proof or prevent the promised recovery semantics.

artifacts.name: security-evidence-review.md
artifacts.content:
# V14 Security And Evidence Review

## Verdict

`redesign`. All eleven declared context sources matched their exact raw SHA-256 and byte bindings. The review found eight material contract defects.

## Trust Model

External trust roots must include the owner-approved specialist compilation and package digest pair, calibration evidence, host inventory, routing policy, assignment approval, override approval, run/session expectation, workspace baseline, and authorized host attestors. Attacker-controlled inputs include inventory records, profile identifiers, costs, capability and independence claims, adapter observations, native handles, launch receipts, lifecycle events, result bytes, RunView text, locators, and replayed artifacts. Core may prove canonical derivation and binding among trusted inputs; it cannot independently prove runtime quality, launch, permission enforcement, process identity, or host observations.

## Prioritized Findings

### S1 - Critical: handoffs are replayable and can be paired with an unrelated launch

V12 handoffs bind goal, agent, blueprint, and compilation but contain no run nonce, attempt identity, launch-command digest, receipt digest, actor authentication, or freshness proof. V14 requires an approved assignment and valid launch receipt before settlement, yet nothing binds the accepted raw handoff to that particular launch. A valid historical handoff for the same package can therefore settle behind a fresh receipt, and a result produced by one runtime can be paired with another runtime's receipt.

Correction: define an externally trusted run expectation and one-use launch authorization binding run/session ID, attempt ID, package and compilation digests, inventory, calibration, policy, assignment, approval or override, workspace baseline, command, agent, and expiry or revision. Define a source-preserving capture envelope binding the exact raw handoff bytes and digest to the command, receipt, attempt, and authorized host attestor. The reducer must reject reused authorization, stale attempts, cross-session replay, and receipt/handoff substitution. Describe this only as authenticated host evidence, not proof that core executed the work.

Required adversarial tests: replay one handoff in another session; pair a handoff with a different receipt, assignment, effort, or agent; replay an authorization; submit a stale receipt after reassignment; and substitute result bytes after capture.

### S2 - Critical: promised escalation conflicts with immutable V12 terminal routing

ADR 0005 makes the first verified non-`pass` handoff terminal, permits one handoff per blueprint, prevents further settlements, and requires retry or replacement to use external evidence or a newly reviewed package. V14 simultaneously promises typed recovery and bounded escalation through a newly approved assignment while claiming V12 remains authoritative. Reassigning the same blueprint cannot implement that promise in the existing session.

Correction: choose and specify one immutable correction model. The smallest coherent option is a new reviewed package or correction generation with a new session identity, explicit predecessor binding, bounded route budget, preserved failed handoff, new assignment and approval, and no mutation of the prior session. Define exact precedence for late parallel results, repeated failures, exhausted attempts, and integration eligibility across generations.

Required adversarial tests: attempt escalation in a terminal V12 session; reuse the old approval; accept a late sibling handoff after routing; exceed the route budget; and omit the failed predecessor evidence from the correction generation.

### S3 - Critical: approval is described but has no external trust boundary

The candidate says approval binds compilation, package, inventory, policy, and assignment digests, but defines no closed approval root, trusted expectation, authentication boundary, freshness, decision state, or one-use launch scope. A digest proves content identity, not owner approval. An attacker can supply an internally consistent self-authored approval or replay approval after an override, inventory revision, workspace change, or new run.

Correction: define a closed `RuntimeAssignmentApproval` and external `AdaptiveRunExpectation`. Bind goal, compilation, package, inventory, calibration, policy, assignment, override state, approver role, decision, run/session, workspace baseline, revision, and validity window or one-use authorization. Require the external expectation on create, restore, inspect, command derivation, receipt acceptance, and settlement. State that the host authenticates the approver while core checks binding and consistency only.

Required adversarial tests: embedded self-approval; wrong approver role; approval for another package, inventory, policy, assignment, run, or workspace; old approval after override; duplicate approval use; unknown fields; and expired or superseded approval.

### S4 - High: inventory quality and independence claims lack immutable calibration evidence and drift protocol

The inventory references only a calibration revision while self-declaring capability tiers and reviewer-independence domains. No digest-bound calibration artifact identifies the assessed profile/effort, catalog and adapter revision, scale, evidence, assessor, applicability, expiry, or revocation. `Catalog drift ... invalidates the launch path` has no normative observation, comparison, or transition. A host can inflate a tier, invent distinct independence labels, reuse a revision, or omit a cheaper feasible profile while still producing a valid inventory.

Correction: introduce immutable calibration evidence bound to exact profile/effort identities, runtime family, catalog and adapter revisions, closed scales, evidence references, assessor authorization, independence-domain semantics, validity, and content digest. Make inventory approval an external trust root and define a prelaunch inventory observation that either matches the approved snapshot or forces recompilation and approval. Claim least cost only within the exact approved inventory; if inventory completeness is asserted, make that an explicit host claim.

Required adversarial tests: altered capability under the same revision; stale calibration; profile aliasing; fabricated independence domains; removed cheaper candidate; changed supported effort; and catalog drift between approval and launch.

### S5 - High: launch and receipt bindings do not prove exact materialization or least authority

The launch command uses broad references, while the receipt records observed profile, effort, tools, skills, native handle, and bounded evidence. It does not normatively bind the approval, override, inventory snapshot, calibration, actual permission grant, isolation configuration, delivered contract/context bytes, workspace source baseline, or applied steering. Inventory support for a permission feature is not evidence that the launch used the required restriction. A correct profile launched with broader filesystem, network, process, or secret authority could pass the described receipt check.

Correction: define closed command and materialization records binding all approved digests, exact workspace/source baseline, exact delivered contract and context byte bindings, normalized tool and skill sets, isolation, permission grants, environment policy, adapter revision, and native parameters. Receipt observations must cover every substitution-sensitive field and reject any widening or mismatch. Semantic steering must be forbidden or represented as a newly approved immutable command; free-form steering cannot silently alter the specialist contract.

Required adversarial tests: correct profile with wrong effort; extra tool, skill, filesystem, network, process, or secret authority; wrong workspace or baseline; changed context bytes; path alias or symlink substitution; adapter substitution; omitted isolation; and unapproved steering.

### S6 - High: no source-preserving adaptive session or restore boundary is defined

V12 preserves the complete package and exact raw handoffs, but V14 adds inventory, calibration, demand, policy, assignments, approvals, overrides, commands, receipts, observations, captures, escalations, and RunView without defining an immutable source-preserving session, raw restore boundary, transition order, or digest registry. A projection containing references and digests cannot reconstruct or reverify the trace when referenced content is absent or mutable.

Correction: define an immutable adaptive session that embeds exact bounded raw bytes or content-addressed immutable values for every decision and observation source. Require an external expectation on every operation. Specify closed JSON shapes, canonical ordering, domain-separated digests, duplicate-key rejection, strict UTF-8, canonical base64, unsafe-text handling, resource limits, cause/prior/successor transition bindings, and deterministic restore. Missing source bytes must block rather than degrade to a summary.

Required adversarial tests: byte-identical restore; missing source; swapped approval or receipt; duplicate JSON keys; malformed UTF-8; noncanonical base64; truncation; reordered events; stale self-digest; and every declared size boundary.

### S7 - High: acceptance criterion AC6 overstates host evidence as proof

The trust boundary correctly says core cannot prove a launch occurred or that the observed handle is a real process. AC6 nevertheless says a launch receipt `proves` what the host attempted and observed. Internal consistency of attacker-controlled host claims is not independent proof and may be rendered misleadingly in RunView.

Correction: rename or specify the receipt as a host-attested claim. Reserve `verified` for schema, digest, authorization, and consistency checks. RunView must visibly separate approved decisions, internally verified bindings, host-claimed effects, independently verified handoffs, and unresolved facts. No state may say running, launched, enforced, or proved from an unauthenticated or merely self-consistent receipt.

Required adversarial tests: forged receipt with valid internal digests; untrusted native handle; lifecycle claim without authorization; renderer assertions for each evidence class; and host claim presented without independent corroboration.

### S8 - High: selection is under-specified as a joint authority and independence decision

The contract describes profile/effort filtering and ordering, but host concurrency and producer/checker independence are properties of the assignment set, not isolated candidates. No exact global assignment-vector ordering or look-ahead rule prevents the cheapest producer choice from consuming the only independence-compatible reviewer supply. This repeats the width-dependent independence risk preserved in Round 4.

Correction: compile the complete assignment vector over all selected blueprints. Hard-gate joint capability, authority, concurrency, availability, and independence feasibility before optimization. Preserve downstream independent-review feasibility, then apply one declared lexicographic objective and canonical vector tie-break. Emit complete rejection reasons without exposing rejected unsafe text.

Required adversarial tests: scarce independence domain; width-one versus wider execution; shared concurrency slot; equal-cost vector tie; unavailable reviewer after producer choice; and override that is locally feasible but globally breaks independence.

## Required Ordering

The fail-closed lifecycle should be: verify external expectation and immutable sources; derive demand; verify calibration and inventory; compile the globally feasible assignment; obtain assignment approval; reobserve inventory and workspace baseline; issue one-use launch authorization and exact command; verify materialization claim; accept bounded lifecycle claims; capture exact raw result bytes; verify the capture-to-launch binding; run V11 handoff verification; record the result through V12 or a newly reviewed correction generation; assess dependency fan-in; integrate and review under owner control. Any mismatch before dispatch blocks. Ambiguity after a claimed launch diagnoses or blocks without retry or settlement.

## Conclusion

The architecture has a sound provider-neutral direction, but its current prose does not close the authority and evidence chain from reviewed inventory through launch to exact handoff. S1 through S3 are release-blocking trust failures; S2 also makes the required recovery behavior unimplementable without an explicit redesign. All findings require normative schemas, transition ordering, and adversarial fixtures before implementation approval.

assumptions: The checked-out source identity was not inspected through Git because the contract forbids Git access; review identity is anchored to the generated contract and the exact declared source digest and byte bindings.
No undeclared approval, calibration, adaptive-session, capture, or escalation contract was assumed to exist.
Host-provided runtime and lifecycle data is treated as a claim unless authenticated by an externally trusted host boundary; authentication still does not make it independent proof.
risks: Without redesign, a stale handoff can be accepted as the result of a fresh approved launch.
Self-authored or replayed approval can satisfy an internally consistent but unauthorized launch path.
The promised typed recovery path cannot coexist with unchanged V12 terminal non-pass semantics.
RunView can overstate mutable host observations as verified execution facts.
followUps: Create normative approval, calibration, launch-authorization, materialization, capture, and adaptive-session schemas with exact digest domains and external expectations.
Choose and document an immutable correction-generation model compatible with V12 before implementing escalation.
Add the adversarial and boundary fixtures enumerated in the review, then freeze and independently review the revised architecture candidate.
